experiment: C0 origin and zero locus on the C0 scale

G1 zero set exists, C0 flat on it.detail: zero set = {r >= r*(theta)} with r* spanning 0.8483..0.9832 (86.3% of the disk); C0 == 0 identically there, so C0-per-zero is a constant and carries no per-zero information

G2 origin is a max, not a zero.detail: V(origin)=26.4333 is the near-maximum of V; the zeros are at r >= r*. Origin and zeros are antipodal, not connected

G3 the 0/0 is NOT removable.detail: one-step limit = the last node's own term; 9 distinct values, spread 6.2154. Path-dependent, so the limit does not exist. Falsifies IF_C0_IS_0_OVER_0.md sec.2/3/9

G4 24.434792 is neither limit nor averag.detail: 24.434792 is the raw unnormalised sum for a hand-picked 2-node context; the document's own average is 3.0543 and the real limits span [0.0346, 6.2500]. It is not the removable value

G5 invariance claim is false.detail: a 0.01 coordinate edit changes the limit, and re-indexing gives 768 distinct values over 2^10 contexts. The value is a function of typed coordinates and of an arbitrary context choice

G6 zeta 0/0 is removable, C0 0/0 is not.detail: the zeta 0/0 is genuinely removable: zeta(s)/zeta(1-s) -> chi(rho) with the limit independent of approach direction (error 8.1e-09 at eps=1e-8). |chi| = 1 then holds on the WHOLE line -- at the zero to 1e-41 and at a non-zero impostor to 1e-41 -- so it is a property of the line and cannot decide RH (PL-22 gate C). Off the line it moves by 0.176, so it is not vacuous as a location identity, only as a zero detector. The real asymmetry with C0 is therefore sharper than the old text claimed: the zeta side HAS a unique removable value and the C0 side has none.

verdict: The zeros of the C0 scale form the region {r >= r*(theta)}, whose inner boundary spans 0.8483 to 0.9832 and is not circular; C0 is identically zero there, so C0-per-zero is a constant. The origin is the near-maximum of V, not a zero, and is antipodal to the zero set. The 0/0 of IF_C0_IS_0_OVER_0.md is path-dependent, so it is not a removable singularity, and 24.434792 is neither its limit nor the average the document defines. Nothing here connects to a Millennium Prize Problem.
